mcmorris_thesis_2023.title: An Experience That Lasts a Lifetime: Building Modernity, Man, and Nation at the YMCA of Montreal's Kamp Kanawana, 1894-1967
mcmorris_thesis_2023.author: Grace McMorris
mcmorris_thesis_2023.archive_used: CURMA (Concordia University Records Management and Archives), YMCA of Montreal fonds P145

chapters.intro: pp.1-21: Historiography, methodology, YMCA London-to-Laurentians overview
chapters.ch1: pp.22-52: 'God's Laboratory' - Christian character, Boys Work, health, gender, sexuality
chapters.ch2: pp.53-79: 'Playing Indian' - Council rings, totem poles, Indian lore, colonialism
chapters.ch3: pp.80-106: 'National Vehicle' - Canoe trips, voyageur myth, L&V Games, 1967 Centennial

founding.date_analysis: 1935 doc: '26th year' (counts from 1910). 1941 broadcast: '48th season' (counts from 1894). Both used contemporaneously.

geography.dam_between_lakes: Between Lake Kanawana and Lake Wilson. Ceremonially opened at end of season (1935 History).

lv_games.arrival_kanawana: 1947 (confirmed: YMCA official history says 78th edition in 2025)

mcmorris_details.format: Last week of summer. Entire camp divided into two teams: voyageurs vs lumbermen.
mcmorris_details.by_1958: Well-developed program: teams decided Friday, captains picked that evening, competition through the week
mcmorris_details.crafts: Voyageurs made model paddles, lumbermen made model axes to wear around necks
mcmorris_details.competitions: War canoe races, capture the flag, medley relays
mcmorris_details.note: This is the origin of the L&V Games tradition. Initially 'Lumberman-Voyageur Week', later became 'L&V Games'.
